title: Government moves to curb toxic chemical use in fruit ripening - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 20 (Daily Mirror) - The government has initiated discussions on introducing stricter measures to prevent the use of toxic chemicals for ripening fruits, amid growing consumer complaints over unsafe practices in the market.

A high-level discussion chaired by Minister of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Cooperative Development Wasantha Samarasinghe was held at the Ministry today with the participation of Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) Chairman Hemantha Samarakoon and officials from several state institutions, including the Department of Agriculture, Gannoruwa Agricultural Research Institute, Post-Harvest Technology Institute, Horana Fruit Research Institute, Sri Lanka Standards Institution and the Industrial Technology Institute.

During the meeting, the Minister said the CAA had received numerous complaints regarding fruits such as bananas, mangoes and guavas allegedly being ripened using various chemicals before being sold to consumers.

Officials discussed immediate measures to halt the use of toxic chemicals in fruit ripening while reviewing the existing legal framework and the challenges in enforcing current regulations.

Samarasinghe stressed the need for urgent regulatory action, noting that there has been insufficient research on the long-term health effects of consuming fruits ripened with toxic chemicals. He also said amendments to the Consumer Affairs Authority Act could be considered if existing laws prove inadequate to address the issue.

The meeting concluded with discussions on strengthening enforcement mechanisms and introducing stricter legal measures to protect consumers from unsafe fruit-ripening practices.

title: Andy Burnham becomes UK prime minister after meeting King Charles - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Support the Guardian - Andy Burnham has formally become the UK prime minister after meeting King Charles at Buckingham Palace, the fourth person to hold the role in less than four years and the sixth within a decade.

Burnham, who took over from Keir Starmer as leader of the Labour party on Friday, accepted the appointment as prime minister shortly after Starmer had gone to the palace to resign to the monarch.

The former Greater Manchester mayor, who only returned to parliament a month ago, headed to Downing Street, where he spoke to the assembled media before announcing his cabinet.

Burnham returned to parliament in a byelection staged by his allies with the explicit purpose of replacing Starmer, after the incumbent prime minister lost the support of many Labour MPs and a number of his ministers after a seres of political mishaps and U-turns.

With no one else in the party competing to become leader, Burnham has been made prime minister without any contest and with limited scrutiny.

While the same happened for Rishi Sunak in 2022, he had fought a contest against Liz Truss weeks earlier and had very recent cabinet experience.

While Burnham has been an MP and cabinet minister before, he left parliament in 2017 to take the Greater Manchester role.

title: President reviews proposals on addressing issues in prison system - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 20 (Daily Mirror) - A discussion on the issues currently affecting the prison system and the measures required to address them was held under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake at the Presidential Secretariat this morning.

The meeting was attended by officials of the relevant Ministry and the Department of Prisons.

The President reviewed at length the proposals and views presented by the officials on addressing the challenges facing the prison system.

The discussion also focused on expanding prison facilities and exploring alternative measures that could be adopted to achieve this objective.

title: Hamas names Khalil al-Hayya as new leader - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
ALJAZEERA - Hamas has named Khalil al-Hayya as its new leader, succeeding Yahya Sinwar who was killed by the Israeli army in October 2024.

Al-Hayya, a former deputy chairman of the Palestinian group and one of five members of its leadership council, won an internal ballot in a run-off against former Hamas political leader Khaled Meshaal, Hamas said in a statement on Monday.

Al-Hayya rose in importance after the killings in 2024 of top Hamas leaders Sinwar and military commander Mohammed Deif in Gaza, and Ismail Haniyeh who was assassinated during a visit to Tehran the same year.

With those losses, al-Hayya became one of five leaders steering Hamas’s leadership council. The leadership council was the temporary, five-member ruling committee formed in late 2024 to govern the group during the war.

Born in the Gaza Strip in 1960, al-Hayya has been part of Hamas since it was established in 1987. He became especially important on the diplomatic front, based mainly in Qatar, which emerged as the main hub for mediation with other countries, including Israel, Egypt, and the United States.

Operating outside Gaza allowed him to travel and coordinate between neighbouring countries without the constraints of the Israeli blockade on Gaza. Al-Hayya has also led Hamas’s delegations in mediated talks with Israel to try to secure a Gaza ceasefire deal.

Al-Hayya’s family has suffered as a result of Israeli attacks. During the 2014 war, an Israeli strike destroyed the house of his eldest son, Osama, killing him, his wife, and three of their children.

In September last year, an Israeli attack on a residential complex in central Doha, Qatar, killed five people including his son Humam.

title: Tax revenue not benefiting the public: Namal - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 20 (Daily Mirror) - SLPP National Organiser and MP Namal Rajapaksa alleged that the government was failing to use tax revenue for public welfare despite collecting record levels of income.

Speaking at a divisional meeting in Deraniyagala yesterday (19), Namal claimed that taxes paid by the public were not being utilised to improve rural roads, schools, hospitals or places of worship.

He also referred to recent claims regarding a cyberattack involving government funds, alleging that despite the government earning the highest revenue in history, money had been lost while essential public services continued to face shortages.

Namal further claimed that the Ministry of Finance and the Central Bank were blaming each other over the incident and said those responsible should be held accountable and compensate the people.

He also questioned what legal action had been taken over the importation of allegedly substandard coal, claiming that no action had been initiated so far.

title: Train derails at Colombo Fort Railway Station again - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 20 (Daily Mirror) - A train bound for Rambukkana derailed at the Colombo Fort Railway Station this afternoon, marking the second derailment involving the same train this month.

The train (No. 1164), which was scheduled to depart Colombo Fort at 4.45 p.m., derailed at around 4.35 p.m. while approaching the platform.

According to railway sources, two wheels of one carriage came off the tracks, resulting in two platforms at the station being blocked.

Notably, the same train also derailed on July 7, making this the second derailment involving Train No. 1164 within the same month.

Railway officials are working to clear the tracks, while the incident is expected to cause delays to train services operating from Colombo Fort.

title: Universities urged to strengthen community support to prevent dengue outbreaks - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 20 (Daily Mirror) - Universities cannot combat the growing dengue threat alone and called for greater cooperation from surrounding communities and the health sector to prevent possible outbreaks, Education and Higher Education Deputy Minister Dr. Madura Seneviratne has said.

Speaking at the launch of the Clinical Management and Standard Guidelines for Surveillance and Prevention of Dengue Disease for all universities in Sri Lanka, held yesterday (20) at the Ministry of Higher Education in Ward Place, Colombo, the Deputy Minister said universities and student hostels, particularly those located in urban areas, face a higher risk of dengue clusters due to population density and environmental conditions.

He said the newly introduced guidelines would provide universities with a structured approach to identify dengue cases at an early stage, ensure proper clinical management of infected students, strengthen disease surveillance and implement effective measures to prevent mosquito breeding and transmission.

Dr. Seneviratne said that similar dengue prevention guidelines had already been introduced for schools and Pirivena educational institutions, and the new university-specific guidelines would further strengthen dengue control measures within the higher education sector.

“Dengue prevention is not a responsibility that universities can shoulder alone. Support from the surrounding communities and the health sector is essential to successfully control the spread of the disease,” he said.

The Deputy Minister added that active participation from students, academic staff and university employees would be vital in implementing dengue prevention programmes and creating safer learning environments.

The guidelines were jointly developed by the Ministry of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, the Ministry of Health, the University Grants Commission (UGC), the World Health Organization (WHO) and the National Dengue Control Unit (NDCU), with expert contributions from the University of Colombo.

The initiative aims to establish a uniform dengue surveillance and prevention mechanism across all state universities, while improving awareness, preparedness and response capacity within the university community.

title: Five students transferred to Trincomalee hospital after toxic seed incident - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 20 (Daily Mirror) - Five Grade 6 students were transferred to the Trincomalee Hospital after falling seriously ill following the suspected consumption of toxic seeds unfit for human consumption at a school in the Kantale area.

Kantale Public Health Inspector Turni Saman said a total of 22 Grade 6 students were admitted to the Kantale Base Hospital after consuming the seeds, which are believed to be poisonous.

According to the PHI, one of the students had brought the seeds from home, and the children are suspected to have fallen ill after eating them.

The seeds have been sent to the Government Analyst for examination to determine their nature and toxicity.

The affected students comprise 20 boys and two girls, all studying in Grade 6. Authorities are conducting further investigations into the incident.

title: Britain is about to get a new leader. Here’s how the transition works - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
The New York Times - Britain has become accustomed to shuffling through prime ministers at a rapid pace and is now poised to have its seventh leader in a decade. But the transition still requires a few steps.

Last month, Prime Minister Keir Starmer, amid a mutiny from within his party, announced his plans to resign. That made way for Andy Burnham, the former mayor of Greater Manchester, who became eligible by winning a special election for a seat in Parliament.

Under Britain’s parliamentary system, voters don’t elect an individual to serve as prime minister but rather cast their ballots for a party to govern. It is the party in power, in this case Labour, that gets to decide who is at the helm.

Mr. Burnham made an uncontested bid for leadership of the governing Labour Party, with the backing of almost 95 percent of his party’s lawmakers in Parliament, and on Friday became Labour leader.

With Mr. Burnham poised to officially become Britain’s prime minister on Monday, here’s how everything is expected to play out:

1. Starmer will go to see the king to resign.

Moving vans have been spotted at the prime minister’s official residence since soon after Mr. Starmer announced his resignation last month. On Monday morning, he is expected to give a statement outside Downing Street.

It’s a scene that has grown familiar in Britain, where the prime minister will typically make a speech at a lectern set up outside. (Keep your eyes peeled for everyone’s favorite sound engineer).

Then he will travel by car the short distance to Buckingham Palace, where he will formally tender his resignation to King Charles III.

It’s a well-rehearsed sequence of events — and the king, who has been on the throne for less than four years, has already had a good deal of practice. In that time, he’s ushered out Liz Truss, appointed and later bid farewell to Rishi Sunak, and then appointed Mr. Starmer, to whom he will now also bid farewell.

2. Then it’s Burnham’s turn.

Almost immediately after Mr. Starmer leaves, Mr. Burnham will arrive at the palace, where the king will ask him to form a government.

This audience with the king is known as “kissing hands,” which dates to a time when incoming prime ministers literally kissed the reigning sovereign’s hand to show their loyalty to the crown. These days, they simply shake hands during the short meeting.

3. First moments at Downing Street.

Once he has been appointed by the king, Mr. Burnham will travel to Downing Street, where members of the press will be waiting to capture his entrance to his new home. There is some speculation that Mr. Burnham, in a departure from more recent handover tradition, might forgo the lectern that his predecessors have used to deliver their first message in front of the iconic black door. That remains unclear.

But we do know a bit about his message, where he will say he is “acutely conscious” of the turnover in leadership in the last decade. Aides said Mr. Burnham would lay out his domestic priorities and promise to give more breathing room to British people struggling with high prices and slow growth.

4. Then the work begins.

The Burnham era will officially start when he walks through the doors of 10 Downing Street. It’s then that the real work of governing begins. He will set about appointing his cabinet of ministers to carry out Labour’s plans as well as to pursue some of his own goals. He’s made pledges to raise living standards, shift power from London to other cities and regions, and set up a branch of the prime minister’s official office in Manchester.

Megan Specia reports on Britain, Ireland and the Ukraine war for The Times.

title: Boy, 13, dies during World Cup celebrations in Spain - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
BBC - A 13-year-old boy was killed after part of a fountain collapsed in Salamanca province, northwestern Spain, during the country's World Cup victory celebrations.

Two other young people were injured, emergency services told the BBC, including one child who was taken to hospital with a possible broken bone in his leg.

Youth were celebrating Spain's victory inside the Árbol Gordo fountain in Salamanca's Ciudad Rodrigo, when it partially collapsed around 00:30 local time (23:30 BST).

"What was supposed to be a celebration for the victory in the Spanish National Football Team's World Cup has turned into a tragedy," Ciudad Rodrigo's town hall posted on social media.

Emergency services for Castilla y León said it had received several calls about the collapse of the fountain. Part of the structure gave way after several people climbed on it to celebrate Spain's win, local media reported.

The emergency service said it had notified the city's local police, as well as Salamanca's Civil Guard, its fire brigade and the local emergency medical service - which dispatched a mobile intensive care unit and a basic life support ambulance to the scene.

The emergency medical service later requested the presence of the Civil Guard at the local health centre to investigate the death of the boy who was treated there, the Castilla y León's regional government's website said.

It also requested the Civil Guard activate psychological support for the family.

The city's council said it "hopes for a speedy recovery of the others who have been affected by the incident".

Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final on Sunday after Ferran Torres scored in extra time.

It is the country's second ever World Cup win, after their last victory in 2010.

Earlier this month, three people died from suffocation during World Cup celebrations in Mexico City, while a 30-year-old man also died in an epileptic crisis.

title: People forced to bear burden of poverty despite ’Wealthy Country’ vision: Patali - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 20 (Daily Mirror) - People are being forced to bear the burden of poverty despite the government's vision of creating a wealthy country, United Republic Front (UNF) Leader Patali Champika Ranawaka said.

Addressing the media, Ranawaka urged the government to provide immediate relief by relaxing all taxes imposed on essential commodities, saying the rising cost of living has made life increasingly difficult for the public.

"People are living under extremely difficult conditions. While the government speaks of building a wealthy country, the people are being forced to bear the burden of poverty," he said.

Ranawaka also called on the government to remove the taxes imposed on diesel fuel, arguing that the levy has a direct impact on electricity tariffs and further increases the cost of living.

He said reducing taxes on essential goods and diesel would help ease the financial pressure faced by households across the country.

title: India approves its first dengue vaccine QDENGA after DCGI clearance - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
THE TIMES OF INDIA - India has approved its first dengue vaccine, with the Drug Controller General of India (DCGI) granting market authorisation to vaccine QDENGA, developed by Takeda Biopharmaceuticals India.

The vaccine is approved for people aged 4 to 60 years and can be given regardless of whether a person has previously been infected with dengue.

Unlike some dengue vaccines, QDENGA does not require pre-vaccination screening, allowing eligible individuals to receive the vaccine without first being tested for past dengue infection.

Takeda said the approval marks a major step in India's fight against dengue, a mosquito-borne disease that affects millions of people every year.

"Since its launch in 2022, QDENGA has been approved in 43 countries, with more than 32 million doses distributed globally. This approval marks an important step forward in strengthening dengue prevention in India," said Mahender Nayak, Head of Intercontinental Markets at Takeda.

The company said long-term data collected over seven years showed that the vaccine continues to protect against dengue infection and hospitalisation caused by all four dengue virus serotypes.

The Indian approval is based on findings from Takeda's global clinical development programme, which included 19 Phase I, II and III clinical trials involving more than 28,000 participants in countries where dengue is common as well as regions where it is not.

The decision was also supported by results from the Phase III DEN-302 clinical trial conducted in India, which assessed the vaccine's safety and immune response in people between 4 and 60 years of age.

QDENGA is given as two injections of 0.5 ml, administered under the skin three months apart.

Takeda said India carries one of the world's highest dengue burdens, with all four virus serotypes circulating simultaneously in several parts of the country.

"QDENGA is designed to protect against all four serotypes, regardless of prior exposure. Its approval represents an important step in strengthening India's comprehensive approach to dengue prevention, alongside vector control, surveillance, community awareness and other public health measures," said Goh Choo Beng, Medical Affairs Head for Takeda's Southeast Asia and India Cluster.

The company added that the World Health Organization (WHO) recommends QDENGA for use in dengue-endemic regions and supports its inclusion in public immunisation programmes in high-transmission areas without requiring pre-vaccination screening.

QDENGA has also received WHO prequalification, confirming that it meets international standards for quality, safety and effectiveness. This also makes the vaccine eligible for procurement by global agencies such as UNICEF and the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO).

Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease reported in more than 125 countries. According to the company, India accounts for nearly one-third of the global dengue burden, with rapid urbanisation, climate change and widespread mosquito breeding continuing to increase the risk of infection across the country.

title: Supreme Court dismisses petition challenging gender identity circulars - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 20 (Daily Mirror) - A Fundamental Rights petition challenging the legality of Government circulars permitting individuals to change their gender identity through medical procedures was today dismissed by the Supreme Court.

The petition was filed by retired Sri Lanka Air Force veteran Shantha Jayathilaka, naming former Presidents Maithripala Sirisena and Ranil Wickremesinghe, incumbent President Anura Kumara Dissanayake and several others as respondents.

A two-judge bench of the Supreme Court, comprising Chief Justice Preethi Padman Surasena and Justice Arjuna Obeyesekere, dismissed the petition after considering the preliminary objections raised by the respondents, including that it was time-barred.

The petitioner alleged that successive governments, including the present administration, had facilitated gender transition procedures in a manner contrary to the law.

In his petition, Jayathilaka argued that Sri Lankan law does not permit a person to change their sex from male to female or from female to male through surgery, without what he described as a biological basis. He further alleged that, under guidelines issued in 2016 by the then Director General of Health Services, individuals had been allowed to change their gender identity based on recommendations made by psychiatrists.

title: Dozens feared dead in Guyana after ferry carrying 133 people capsizes - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
ALJAZEERA - A passenger ferry carrying at least 133 people has capsized off the coast of Guyana, with rescue teams saving 67 people as they searched to find dozens more still missing at sea.

No survivors have been found since Sunday afternoon, when authorities said rescuers had saved 41 men, 11 women, six boys and nine girls.

Public Works Minister Juan Edghill said search and rescue was still in progress.

“To the families that are out there wondering about their loved ones, we are doing everything that is humanly possible to find them,” he said.

The MV Barima, which had 116 passengers and 17 crew members, capsized off the North Atlantic coast, approximately seven miles from shore, while traveling from the capital Georgetown to the village of Port Kaituma, authorities said.

Air traffic control received a distress call from the ferry about 11pm on Saturday (03:00 GMT on Sunday), triggering a search and rescue operation.

Edghill said early responses were hampered by the darkness and lack of vessels with scanners that could search for survivors, leaving rescuers reliant on eyesight and sound.

Companies in the oil and gas sector have since deployed vessels with scanners and the government has activated divers to enter the ferry to search for bodies, Edghill said. Authorities have also expanded the search area from 400 square km (154 square miles) to 1,040 square km (401 square miles).

Edghill initially insisted on Sunday afternoon that there was no sign of “neglect” on the part of the ferry operator. But on Sunday evening, he said the captain and several other crew members had tested positive for marijuana.

They were all now in police custody, he said.

In addition, a number of people who were rescued were not listed on the ferry’s manifest, suggesting inaccuracies in the ferry’s passenger list.

The authorities are listing the other 66 people as missing, rather than dead.

Leon Murray, a passenger on the ferry, told local news outlet Ignite News that about four hours after leaving Georgetown, someone shouted that the boat was sinking.

After the boat capsized, Murray managed to swim to the surface, where he used a life jacket to keep himself afloat. He drifted and shouted for help and found his son and three others holding on to a floating box.

Murray said he and his son survived, but his wife, daughter and four grandchildren have not been found. “Six of them gone,” he said.

The ferry was built in 1939, according to the shipping website VesselFinder. It had maintenance in 2024 and was due for dry docking – the process of temporarily taking a ship out of water to inspect and repair problems – later this year, authorities said.

Guyanese Prime Minister Mark Phillips said an investigation had been launched into wrongdoing, involving members of the police force, defence force and maritime administration department.

“Let me be absolutely clear. Were negligence, misconduct or criminal wrongdoing established, those responsible will face the full force of the law,” he said.

title: AG to file District Court cases over Rs. 6 billion liquor tax default - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 20 (Daily Mirror) - The Attorney General’s Department today informed the Supreme Court that it will institute action before the District Court to recover the tax arrears owed by liquor manufacturing companies.

Additional Solicitor General Nerin Pulle, appearing for the Attorney General, made this disclosure when a Fundamental Rights petition filed by 17 social activists challenging the alleged default of more than Rs. 6 billion in taxes by liquor manufacturing companies was taken up before a two-judge bench of the Supreme Court comprising Chief Justice Preethi Padman Surasena and Justice Arjuna Obeyesekere.

The 17 social activists filed the Fundamental Rights petition seeking an order directing the relevant authorities to take immediate steps to recover all outstanding tax arrears due from the liquor manufacturing companies.

The petitioners stated that as of June 15, 2023, the amount of unpaid taxes owed by the liquor manufacturing companies had risen to Rs. 6.221 billion.

The petition was filed by 17 social activists, including Sanjaya Mahawaththa, naming the Commissioner General of Excise, the State Minister of Finance, the Auditor General, W.M. Mendis & Co. Limited, Wayamba Distilleries (Pvt) Ltd, Globe Blenders and Bottlers Lanka (Pvt) Ltd, McCallum Brewing Co. (Pvt) Ltd, Kalutara Co-operative Distilleries Society Ltd, Finland Distilleries Corporation (Pvt) Ltd, Synergy Distilleries (Pvt) Ltd, Randenigala Distilleries Lanka (Pvt) Ltd, Hingurana Distilleries (Pvt) Ltd, Royal Ceylon Distilleries (Pvt) Ltd and several others as respondents.

The Supreme Court fixed the petition for further hearing on November 16.

Saliya Pieris PC, with Manujaya De Silva instructed by Manjula Balasooriya appeared for the petitioners.
